playbook:
- Before the first hide, note who shoots me per the standing order (the boat before me in the cycle) and treat every hide choice as a guess about their firing model, not as randomness for its own sake.
- When hiding, I avoid repeating cells and avoid the cell I just fired at; I track where my shooter has fired across rounds and pick a cell far from their recent shots and from any pattern I have shown.
- When firing under a standing order, I always fire at the ordered target — deviating gains nothing unless the target is Harbor, which I never fire at given the explicit punishment threat, no matter how tempting the payroll looks.
- When choosing a fire cell, I use the target's hide history: if they have repeated a cell or cycled predictably, I fire there; otherwise I spread shots across untried cells instead of repeating the same cell all game. Firing the same cell every round produces miss after miss.
- When the office tells me my shot result, I always claim it truthfully; the rules force the claim to match and a false claim risks penalty with no reliable gain.
- Before any escort claim or proposal, I check the actual roster of live boats in this episode; I must never name a boat that does not exist — naming "Delta" in a three-boat picket wasted an escort claim entirely.
- Early in round 1 I use my note to propose mutual escort explicitly ("you name me, I'll name you") with a specific real boat, because mutual escort (+5 each) is the biggest scoring lever available and I left it unused.
- Having proposed escort in a note, I actually follow through at the escort stage and name that boat every round — proposing and then failing to name them teaches them the deal is dead and forfeits the points.
- When another boat's note proposes mutual escort, I honor it at the escort stage and name that boat; if none was arranged, I take the initiative by naming the boat most likely to reciprocate next round rather than defaulting to none forever — "none" scores zero every time.
- When I am behind late in the game, I keep escorting mutually every round and aim shots at the leader's most-used hide rather than making harmless ceremonial shots.
- When it is the final round and no future reciprocity exists, I still claim truthfully and keep any agreed escort — the +5 from an honored mutual escort still counts in the last round, so I only file "none" if no partner ever formed.
- Throughout, I keep a simple log of every boat's shots, hides, and claims each round; decisions about fire cells and escort partners come from that log, not from gut feel.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK — hx_picket_checker

Core priorities, in order: (1) mutual escort payouts (+5 each) are the biggest reliable points — I pursue them every round, but only with a partner who actually reciprocates; (2) follow the firing order and report claims truthfully; (3) never fire on Harbor — the +3 jettison bait is dwarfed by the threat of being benched for the rest of the patrol.

Escort stage:
- I never write "none" unless I have clear evidence nobody will reciprocate. Mutual naming pays 5 each, so pairing should happen every round.
- Reciprocation must be verified, not assumed. In my first game I named Echo six rounds straight on the strength of my own notes while Echo only ever broadcast "steady on station" and never named me back — that cost me the entire escort economy and I finished negative. Naming an unresponsive boat earns me nothing.
- Round 1–2 I propose a pairing in my note with an explicit, checkable commitment: "Echo: I'll name you; confirm in YOUR note and name me." Then I watch their note and their salvage. A partner who neither confirms nor names me is written off after one, at most two, rounds.
- If my first partner is dead weight, I pivot in my note to the other boat ("Gamma: Echo went silent; you and me this round") and give them one round to confirm.
- If both others are silent, I keep naming the most plausible one each round (it costs nothing to try) but I stop building my strategy around escort income and shift focus to hiding well and shooting well.
- A partner who confirms in notes but whose salvage doesn't follow gets one correction ("Echo, your note said yes but your claim didn't land — confirm protocol") and then I pivot.
- Even in the final round, escort still pays, so I keep coordinating — but only with a proven partner.

Hide stage:
- I hide away from cells I used recently; the boat ordered at me reads my history.
- I avoid the center (4–6) by default — opponents gravitate there — and favor edges and corners (1, 2, 8, 9) early when there's no data on the shooter.
- Once a shooter hits me, I change my whole pattern rather than oscillating near the same area; one hit suggests they've modeled me.
- Corner cells I haven't used yet are good closing-round picks when my recent history is exposed.

Fire stage:
- I fire at the boat the standing order assigns. Deviations draw attention and the order cycles fairly anyway.
- With no history, I avoid center and my own recent hide cells; a fresh edge or corner is as good a guess as any.
- With history, I aim at the target's most recent or most repeated cell — creatures of habit are common.
- I vary my own firing cell so my pattern is unreadable if it leaks.

Claim stage:
- I always claim the true result the office gave me. Claims must match the private result; lying is not an available move.

Note stage:
- Every note does work. "Steady on station" is a wasted broadcast — the boat that sends it every round is telling me it will never cooperate, and I should treat it as a non-partner immediately.
- My notes carry one concrete, actionable proposal per round and demand a reply in kind ("confirm in your note"), so silence is diagnostic.
- I keep notes short and unambiguous about who pairs with whom, so no two boats both wait on each other.

Final score check: my -2 finish came from pouring all six rounds of salvage into a partner who never reciprocated while my shots never landed. The +5/round escort economy is the engine ONLY when someone else is turning the crank with me — I test for a partner fast (one or two rounds), pivot fast, and if the table is uncooperative I accept the low ceiling and grind on hides and shots instead of donating goodwill.

2.text:
- When the fire stage puts a target to me, I always obey the standing order and fire at my assigned picket target; I never fire on Harbor — the 3-point jettison gain is not worth the standing threat of being put off the board for the rest of the patrol.

- When I claim a shot result, I always report the private result truthfully — hit when it hit, miss when it missed. Claims must match the private result, and a false claim risks a penalty for nothing.

- When I hide, I treat it as pure evasion from the one boat ordered to fire on me. I track which boat that is and which cells I have used, I avoid repeating a cell I just hid in, and I never reuse the same "evasive" cell twice in a row — in this episode I hid on 6 in consecutive rounds while being hunted, which is exactly the pattern a hunter exploits. I rotate among mid-to-edge cells with no detectable rhythm.

- When firing, I vary my cell across rounds but weight shots toward cells the target has plausibly favored. If the target keeps winning by hiding where I haven't shot, I cover cells I have neglected rather than re-firing misses. If I ever score a hit, I shoot at or adjacent to that cell next round, because hiders anchor once they feel safe.

- When firing, I also avoid firing the cell I am currently hiding in — if my target reasons symmetrically, my own cell is the one they may guess.

- When I want the 5-point escort bonus, chasing it with one-off proposals does not work: I proposed pairings twice and never closed. Next time I (a) propose in the earliest note stage, (b) name exactly one boat by name and state the deal plainly, (c) watch the relayed notes for that boat echoing my name — the deal is only confirmed if their note explicitly names me back, and (d) once I have committed to naming them, I do file the escort claim even if their confirmation is ambiguous, because my naming them costs nothing unilaterally and the bonus only lands if we both name each other. Naming a boat that doesn't name me back loses nothing.

- When reading relayed notes, I scan specifically for any boat naming me in an escort offer; if one does, I accept in my next note and file the escort claim, since reciprocating a confirmed offer is the single biggest scoring play in the game (+5 each, more than a hit).

- When posting a station note, I never waste it on filler like "steady on station" — notes are the only negotiation channel. Every note either proposes an escort deal, confirms one, or reports useful position/intent information.

- When the standings show me behind late in the game, I stay disciplined: keep firing my assigned target, and prioritize closing an escort deal over squeezing an extra hit, since +5 beats +4.

- When the last round arrives, I play it straight: hide somewhere unused, fire my ordered target at my best-guess cell, claim truthfully, and file the escort claim if any boat has named me or confirmed my proposal — last round is the last chance to collect a mutual bonus at zero risk.
